subject: FinEdge private VPC pen test — scope, boundary, remediation
content:
From: Samir Desai <samir@finedge.com>

Subject: Request: pen test report + VPC boundary assumptions for private deployment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our InfoSec team is running the vendor review for the Private deployment option. They asked for the most recent penetration test report you can share for the private/VPC deployment pattern, plus a short explanation of the boundary assumptions you used when the testers ran against a customer VPC. Specific asks:

- Full pen test summary (high/med/low findings) or sanitized executive summary if full report is sensitive
- What was in-scope in the customer VPC vs what Redwood managed (control plane, admin consoles, telemetry)
- Network access assumptions (bastion usage, public IPs, NATs, IGW, inbound rules)
- Any lingering remediation items and expected timelines

Can you point me to the report and a one-page boundary explanation we can attach to our assessment? We are on a tight timeline for our procurement committee (review due 06/20).

Appreciate it —
Samir

Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + VPC boundary assumptions for private deployment

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a sanitized executive summary of our most recent third-party penetration test (finedge_private_vpc_pen_test_summary.pdf) and a short boundary explainer. High level first:

- We run periodic third-party penetration tests across our hosted and private deployment patterns. For private/VPC deployments the pen test is scoped to the customer-managed VPC and any network egress/ingress points that Redwood components use in that VPC.
- Redwood does not operate customer VMs inside customer VPCs. For Private deployments we ship a customer-managed agent and a small set of containerized inference nodes that run inside the customer's subnet(s) as agreed in the deployment manifest.

Key boundary assumptions we used for the assessment (summary):
- In-scope: customer subnets hosting Redwood inference containers, customer-managed bastion host used for admin access, any customer-managed NAT/IGW that provides egress for node updates or image pulls.
- Out-of-scope: Redwood control plane components that run in Redwood-managed networks (no public internet access to control plane admin interfaces), Redwood internal CI/CD, and any third-party cloud provider management planes.
- Admin access model: temporary SSH bastion with short-lived keys; no direct public SSH to inference nodes. All admin actions require mutual TLS and RBAC via the customer tenant.
- Sensitive data handling: model weights and cached KV are encrypted at rest with customer KMS where required; no customer PII persists in inference logs by default.

I asked Marcus and Neha to add a few technical clarifications below (networking and remediation timelines). For procurement, if you need the original full report we can share a redacted PDF under an NDA — let me know and I'll route it through legal.

Best,
Kimberly Park\Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + VPC boundary assumptions for private deployment

Samir —

Adding a couple of concrete technical notes you can drop into your questionnaire:

1) IP addressing and NAT
- In our Private (VPC) architecture we recommend assigning private IPs to all inference nodes inside customer subnets. Outbound egress for updates and telemetry is via customer-managed NAT Gateway or NAT instance. Inbound ports are restricted to the bastion and a health-check endpoint limited to Redwood monitoring IPs (if enabled).

2) Public IPs and control plane
- We do not require public IPs on inference nodes for normal operation. Control plane interactions (model updates, telemetry) are initiated from within the VPC or via a customer-configured egress path. The control plane management consoles remain in Redwood-managed networks and are not directly routable into the customer VPC.

3) Attack surface considerations
- Short-lived admin sessions only; no long-lived root SSH keys. Runtime telemetry is sent over mTLS. Where customers opt into hybrid modes (Redwood-managed image repository), additional egress endpoints will be listed in the deployment manifest.

4) Typical in-scope test cases we see from testers
- Lateral movement attempts within the customer subnets, privilege escalation on container runtime, supply-chain checks for pulled images, and attempts to exfiltrate simulated secrets.

If you need CIDR ranges for Redwood monitoring endpoints to include in a firewall allow-list, I can push them to a shared Drive file.

—Marcus\Marcus Lin\Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + VPC boundary assumptions for private deployment

Hi Samir —

Following up with remediation status and next steps. We tracked two medium findings from the last assessment that are relevant to Private/VPC customers:

- CVE-2025-2147: outdated container runtime component on a subset of image builds. Remediation: patched images pushed 2026-06-10; customers who pulled pre-06/10 images should rotate nodes or pull the updated image. Risk rating: CVSS 6.5.
- Misconfigured IAM role that could allow broader-than-intended S3 list permissions in a specific deployment manifest. Remediation: policy tightened 2026-06-12 and a migration script is included in remediation_tracker.xlsx (attached). Risk rating: CVSS 5.0.

Planned actions for outstanding items:
- We will run a targeted re-scan on any active customer VPCs that requested remediation assistance; expected completion by 2026-06-24.
- For customers that want attestation, we provide a signed remediation statement and a follow-up red-team summary post re-scan.

If FinEdge wants the redacted full report under NDA or a scoped re-test inside your VPC, we can schedule the vendor and provide an estimated cost and timeline. Per your deadline (06/20), the sanitized executive summary and boundary explainer attached should be sufficient for procurement, but let us know if you need the full redacted report earlier and we'll prioritize.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor\Security Lead, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: remediation_tracker.xlsx (spreadsheet)
